misconceptions.description: Thinking a couple produces a nonzero resultant force
misconceptions.trigger: learner adds the two equal and opposite forces as if they reinforce each other
misconceptions.feedback: A couple contains two equal and opposite forces, so the net force is zero. The remaining mechanical effect is a moment only.

misconceptions.description: Using the wrong distance in the couple-moment formula
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses a diagonal or arbitrary point distance instead of perpendicular separation
misconceptions.feedback: In M = Fd for a couple, d must be the perpendicular distance between the lines of action of the two forces.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a force can be moved anywhere without adding a couple
misconceptions.trigger: learner relocates a force and claims the system is unchanged
misconceptions.feedback: A couple is a free vector, but a force is not. Moving a force to a different line of action requires an added couple to preserve equivalence.
